message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to cancel a date because I'm really tired. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I've been talking to this guy for two weeks, and we had our first date a week after we started talking. That went well, and then we had our second date on Wednesday. Now it's Friday in Australia, and we were supposed to have our third date tonight to watch a movie. On the second date, I mentioned that some of the things she said over the last week had been a bit overwhelming because she was planning too far ahead. I wanted to be transparent but also let her know that it hadn't freaked me out, and I just wanted to take things slow. She understood, and we made plans to hang out on Friday night again to watch a movie. But here's the thing: I've had an incredibly long week. I only got about four hours of sleep and worked from 7 am to 5 pm with only a half-hour break. By the time she asked me around 5:30 pm if we were grabbing dinner or if she should get something herself, I felt horrible. I told her I was absolutely shattered and would probably just fall asleep. I asked if we could do it on Sunday instead, offering to take her out to lunch and pay for it, and we could watch a movie then. Now, I'm worried that she might think I'm not interested anymore, especially since I already mentioned that I wanted to take things slow. I'm wondering if I'm being petty by rescheduling the date because I'm tired, or if it's reasonable. I don't want her to think I'm trying to get out of the relationship or that I'm not interested anymore. I guess I need to consider a few things here. First, is it okay to cancel a date because of exhaustion? I mean, everyone has off days, and it's important to take care of yourself. But at the same time, communication is key in a relationship. I told her I was tired and asked to reschedule, which seems honest. But maybe she feels like I'm not making an effort or that I'm not prioritizing our time together. Also, I mentioned earlier that I wanted to take things slow because her planning ahead was a bit much for me. Does that mean I'm setting expectations that I need to stick to? If I'm inconsistent with my actions, like saying I want to take things slow but then rescheduling because of tiredness, does that send mixed signals? I'm also thinking about how she might perceive this. If she's already had doubts about me because of my initial comment about taking things slow, rescheduling the date might reinforce those doubts. She might think I'm not that interested or that I'm trying to distance myself. On the other hand, I don't want to force myself to go out when I'm exhausted. That could lead to a bad time for both of us, and it's not fair to either of us to be half-present. It's important to maintain a balance between self-care and being attentive to the relationship. Maybe I should have communicated my tiredness earlier or found another way to spend time together that's less demanding. But I didn't, and now I'm stuck with this situation. I need to decide whether it's better to go through with the date despite being tired or to reschedule and risk her thinking I'm not interested. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Could I have suggested a different activity that's less energy-consuming? Or could I have asked her to be understanding about my current state? It's possible that she would have been more understanding if I had framed it differently or provided more context about why I'm tired. In the end, I think it's important to be honest and upfront about my needs while also being considerate of her feelings. Maybe I should reach out to her again to clarify my intentions and reassure her that I'm still interested, but just need a bit of time to rest. That way, I can address her potential concerns and maintain the trust in our relationship. But I'm still not sure if this is the right approach. I don't want to over-explain or come off as defensive, but I also don't want her to feel neglected or unimportant. It's a delicate balance, and I'm not entirely confident in how to navigate it perfectly. I guess I'll have to weigh the importance of self-care against the importance of maintaining a healthy relationship. If I consistently prioritize my tiredness over our time together, it might send the wrong signals. But if I push myself too hard, it could lead to resentment or burnout. In conclusion, while it's understandable to want to reschedule due to exhaustion, it's crucial to communicate effectively and reassure her of my interest in the relationship. That way, I can maintain trust and ensure that she doesn't misinterpret my actions as a lack of interest.
